newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers' head renews attack on government.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers' head renews attack on government.

text.p: The head of the Italian employers' federation renewed an attack on the government on Wednesday, saying if it failed to proceed with plans to clean up Italy's finances the ensuing crisis would sweep Italy away.

Confindustria chairman Giorgio Fossa, who criticised the government at the weekend for tax hikes in its 1997 budget, slammed Rome's efforts to improve public finances as it tries to squeeze Italy in at the start of Europe's monetary union.

Speaking at a presentation of Confindustria's economic forecasts, Fossa reinforced a similar warning he made at the weekend, saying if the government did not meet its objectives in cutting Italy's bloated budget deficit "it will be the national crisis, and not us in business, which will sweep it away."
"Like all buildings constructed on sand, even the bricks of this, as of any other government, risk being blown away in the first gale," he said.

He referred to the three percent ratio of budget deficit to gross domestic product required as one criteria for countries wanting to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) at its planned 1999 start.

"What will happen when the markets discover that the budget will not guarantee the three percent ratio between deficit and GDP, that the 1997 deficit will be higher than expected and that pensions spending remains out of control?" he said.
Fossa, at the weekend, criticised the government for raising taxes in the 1997 budget rather than making it easier for industry to create jobs.
His criticisms were echoed by Cesare Romiti, chairman of Italian car giant Fiat, who said the government needed to relaunch the economy and stem fears of unemployment.
